title: PV Sindhu Wins Japan Open Title, Becomes First Indian to Claim the Crown
excerpt: The two-time Olympic medalist defeated home favorite Akane Yamaguchi 21-17, 21-17 in the final for her first major title since the 2022 Singapore Open.
body:
• PV Sindhu defeated Japan's Akane Yamaguchi 21-17, 21-17 to win the Japan Open women's singles title on Sunday — the first Indian to claim the crown at the prestigious BWF Super 750 event.
  • The title is Sindhu's first major triumph since winning the Singapore Open in 2022 and her first tour-level title since the Syed Modi International in December 2024.
  • The 31-year-old former world champion is now projected to rise to World No. 9, having started the year ranked 18th.
  • The victory provides a timely boost ahead of the BWF World Championships in New Delhi from August 17-23.

PV Sindhu won the Japan Open women's singles title on Sunday, defeating home favorite Akane Yamaguchi 21-17, 21-17 in the final at the Tokyo Metropolitan Gymnasium. She became the first Indian to win the prestigious BWF Super 750 tournament.

The victory marks a resurgence for the 31-year-old, whose last major title came at the Singapore Open in 2022. Her most recent tour-level crown was the Syed Modi International Super 300 in December 2024.

"This is what I fight for. The flag. My country."

— PV Sindhu, on Instagram after winning the title

A Week of Dominant Badminton

Sindhu's path to the title was commanding. She opened with a straight-games win over Malaysia's Wong Long Ching (21-14, 21-17), then dismantled China's world No. 5 Han Yue in just 35 minutes (21-16, 21-14). A walkover in the quarterfinals against the injured Nozomi Okuhara gave her extra recovery time before the semifinals.

In the last four, she ended a five-match losing streak against China's Chen Yufei, the former Olympic champion, taking the opening game 21-19 and building a 15-10 lead in the second before Chen retired with a hamstring injury. Their last meeting won by Sindhu came during the 2019 BWF World Championships, where she claimed the world title.

Against Yamaguchi, ranked world No. 3, Sindhu fell behind early in the opening game but fought back to seize control. She carried that momentum through both games, sealing the title in straight sets.

Rising Through the Rankings

Sindhu began 2026 ranked world No. 18. After the Japan Open, she is projected to climb to No. 9 — a significant jump that reflects her third semifinal appearance of the year, following strong runs at the Malaysia Open Super 1000 and Australia Open Super 500.

The two-time Olympic medalist — she won silver at Rio 2016 and bronze at Tokyo 2020 — remains India's most decorated badminton player. The Japan Open title adds another chapter to a career that includes a world championship gold and multiple Super Series crowns.

Eyes on New Delhi

The timing is significant. The BWF World Championships begin on August 17 in New Delhi, giving Sindhu a chance to compete for a second world title on home soil. She won her only world championship gold in 2019 in Basel, Switzerland, and the Super 750 victory suggests she is peaking at the right moment.

Sindhu was the only Indian player remaining at the Japan Open this year. Lakshya Sen and Ayush Shetty exited in the opening round. The men's doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty retired hurt in their first match, and the mixed doubles duo of Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto fell in the pre-quarterfinals.
